# PR:121 — release 1.8.0 (merged)

Date: 2026-11-21
Status: merged 2026-11-21 13:40 UTC (merge commit `50daccc`); v1.8.0 published

## Intent

Release Please PR for 1.8.0, created 2026-11-08. Six files:
`.release-please-manifest.json` (1.7.1 to 1.8.0), `CHANGELOG.md`,
`CITATION.cff`, `rust/signal-core/Cargo.toml`,
`rust/signal-core/Cargo.lock`, `version.txt`.

## Review

- Changelog contents match the merged commits since `v1.7.1`:
  outgoing and incoming link previews (`a3dc43b`, `7abe466`,
  `cc17d3e`), store-transience fixes (`901142b`, `3b58d8a`,
  `4696b31`), presage batched pre-key saves (`ead095c`), and test
  Git-environment isolation (`92f2cff`, `c854175`, `19aa464`).
- No unexplained or unrelated changes. All PR checks pass
  (build-and-test, debian-13-build-and-install,
  ubuntu-24-04-build-and-install, CodeQL, dependency review).
- The PR predates `56916ef` (PR:125, docs-only maintainer brief), so
  Release Please has not re-run against it. No `autorelease:` label.
- `release-please-config.json` carries no `publish` override; the
  Release Please App token has `contents: write`, so merging the PR
  creates the tag and draft release itself, after which the
  `release-artifacts` workflow builds, packages, and publishes.

## Decision

Held after explicit approval on 2026-11-21. The remaining live
verification items from
`work/prekey-misalignment-handover-2026-11-14.md` (bootup contention
without "Bad encrypted message", link preview thumbnail receipt,
tests 3-9) are still open. The release is a draft, so a follow-up
patch release remains possible if live validation surfaces a defect.

## Update 2026-11-21 (after Dependabot merges)

Merging PR:126/127/128 pushed `b239d1e`, `879ee56`, and `cff15d7`
to `main`. The Release Please workflow re-ran on the final push and
regenerated the PR head in place (new single commit `f8ffa8e4`,
updated 12:01 UTC).

Regeneration caveat: the new head's `Cargo.lock` is based on the
pre-bump dependency state. The diff now reverts `zeroize` from 1.9.2
to 1.9.1 (checksum included). The sqlx 0.9.1 entry, the
`libredox`/`objc2-core-foundation` additions, and the `sha2`
deduplication from PR:127 are absent from the regenerated lock.

Consequence: merging the regenerated PR would revert the zeroize
bump already on `main`. Release Please's extra-files handling
rewrites `Cargo.lock` from the manifest baseline rather than the
current `main` state.

## Update 2026-11-21 (lock fix, approved)

Lock regression resolved by hand. Fetched the regenerated head
(`f8ffa8e4`), rebased it onto current `main` (`8ed04b7`), and
amended the release commit: `cargo update -p zeroize` restored
zeroize 1.9.2. The lock now matches `main` exactly except the
signal-core version bump (1.7.1 to 1.8.0); sqlx 0.9.1 and all
transitive entries are intact. Pushed as new head `126a286`
(force-with-lease onto the Release Please branch, plus a backup
branch `maintainer/release-1.8.0-lock-fix`).

PR:121 is now mergeable with a correct lock. Merging publishes
v1.8.0: tag, draft release, and the `release-artifacts` workflow
(build, package, APT publish) run on the merge.

## Update 2026-11-21 (merged, published)

Merged with `gh pr merge --merge` at 13:40 UTC (merge commit
`50daccc`). All nine checks green on the fixed head. The Release
Please workflow on the merge created tag `v1.8.0` and the release;
the `release-artifacts` workflow then built, packaged, and attached
all eight artifacts (Debian 13 + Ubuntu 24.04 debs, dbgsym debs,
x86_64 rpm, orig tarball, SPDX SBOM, SHA256SUMS), and the
`publish-apt-repository` step dispatched the protected APT
publication, which completed successfully (run 44913479717).

The release was promoted from draft to published (no
`autorelease:` label, so Release Please published it directly on
merge). Post-merge Release Please re-ran on `50daccc` and was a
no-op (no release commits since the bump); CI on the merge commit
is green.

Residual live verification (tests 3-9 in
`work/prekey-misalignment-handover-2026-11-14.md`) remains open;
if a defect surfaces, a v1.8.1 patch release is the remediation
path.
